answer: Escrowed Interaction Depth. New identities get near-zero outbound reach and must earn it by sustaining reciprocal traffic over time. Each identity's reach is proportional to a slowly accumulating score anchored to distinct counterparties, with decay resetting dormant accounts. A sybil cluster gains little because internal chatter stays umber-colored, flagged as low-entropy and discounted. To fake depth, an attacker must operate real counterparties, paying ongoing compute, latency, and opportunity cost per identity—roughly a monthly jetty fee plus lost throughput—while the reach curve lags,
